projectState.overview: StreamTube is a YouTube-like video sharing platform built as an MBA greenfield challenge. Monorepo with a NestJS 11 backend (nestjs-project/) and a Next.js 16 frontend (next-frontend/). Phases 01 (base config), 02 (auth — backend + frontend) and 03 (video upload and processing) are fully implemented, tested and merged into main. The current branch fix/channel-info delivered a documentation-only correction (COMPLETE): the prose route tables described GET /videos/:publicId as returning 'channel info', but the implementation (VideosService.findByPublicId) returns no channel data — only id, public_id, title, status, duration, thumbnail_url, created_at. The full project workflow was followed (research → plan → implement, artifacts under docs/research + docs/plans). The single functional edit is one line in nestjs-project/CLAUDE.md:170; openapi.json, the controller/service, and the phase-03 plan were already correct and untouched. No production code changes involved. Branch is ready to commit and merge.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 01 — Base Configuration
implementedFeatures.summary: Full project foundation: monorepo structure, NestJS 11 initialized, Docker Compose with PostgreSQL + Mailpit, TypeORM with DataSource and migration runner, environment validation via Joi, namespaced config with registerAs, Swagger/OpenAPI export, ESLint + Prettier.
implementedFeatures.notes: All services use Docker Compose service names as hosts (never localhost). Migrations run via npm run migration:run. Config organized per domain in src/config/ using registerAs factories.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 02 — Auth Backend (NestJS)
implementedFeatures.summary: Full authentication system: user registration with email confirmation, login with JWT access+refresh tokens, logout, forgot/reset password flow, channel auto-creation from email prefix. All flows tested with unit + integration + E2E tests.
implementedFeatures.notes: Backend login/refresh return access_token + refresh_token in the JSON response body; the NestJS API sets no cookies. The HttpOnly cookie is held by the Next.js BFF (iron-session), not the API. Refresh token rotation implemented. Channel nickname derived from email prefix. ChannelsService owns channel creation; UsersService compensates by deleting user if channel creation fails. Public decorator skips JWT guard. DomainException with custom filter.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 02 — Auth Frontend (Next.js)
implementedFeatures.summary: Auth screens built with Next.js App Router: signup, login, forgot-password. BFF API routes proxy to NestJS backend. Session managed via iron-session HttpOnly cookies. RHF + Zod validation. MSW mocks for all auth routes in test. Playwright E2E tests.
implementedFeatures.notes: OpenAPI types generated into lib/api/types.gen.ts. MSW enabled via MSW_ENABLED=true env var at server startup. Design system: Tailwind CSS 4, custom UI primitives in components/ui/. Playwright for E2E tests, Vitest for unit tests.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — Video Upload & Processing (complete, merged to main)
implementedFeatures.summary: End-to-end video pipeline across all 9 SIs: S3 multipart upload for files up to 10GB (initiate, presign-part, complete, abort), BullMQ video-processing queue, a dedicated FFmpeg worker container that extracts metadata (ffprobe) and generates a thumbnail (ffmpeg) then marks the video READY/ERROR, presigned-GET 302 redirects for streaming and download, and a public video-info endpoint.
implementedFeatures.notes: Video status model (enum values: draft, processing, ready, error): create -> DRAFT; completeUpload -> PROCESSING; worker -> READY or ERROR (with error_reason). There is no UPLOADING or FAILED state. publicId is an 11-char nanoid (varchar(11) column). VideoProcessor extends WorkerHost from @nestjs/bullmq v12 and routes by job.name; registered ONLY in WorkerModule. FfmpegService wraps child_process.execFile with an explicit Promise for testability. Stream/download use @Redirect + @Public with a dynamic presigned URL (302). GET /videos/:publicId (findByPublicId) returns ONLY id, public_id, title, status, duration, thumbnail_url, created_at — it does NOT load or return any channel data (no relations in the findOne query).

implementedFeatures.name: task-startup-infra — Docker startup/infra reliability fix (implemented, committed)
implementedFeatures.summary: Clean `docker compose up -d --build` is now operational from a fresh clone on any host. Delivered via 4 committed SIs: S3/Redis blocks in .env.example, a one-shot minio-init bucket-provisioning container, npm ci baked into images with node_modules isolated from the bind mount, and the worker's Video relation graph registered so its DataSource resolves relations.
implementedFeatures.notes: Commits c880433 (SI-1 .env.example S3/Redis), 0f5d099 (SI-2 minio-init one-shot container), b0f8644 (SI-3 npm ci in images + anonymous node_modules volume), d6afe2f (SI-4 WorkerModule TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Video, Channel, User])).

implementedFeatures.name: task-presigned-url-public-endpoint — Presigned URL public endpoint fix (FULLY IMPLEMENTED, committed fa65e83; merged context)
implementedFeatures.summary: Presigned S3/MinIO URLs (upload PUT, stream GET, download GET, thumbnail GET) are now signed with a configurable public endpoint so external clients (browser, frontend, host curl) can use them without curl --resolve. SI-1 added S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT env var + Joi validation + publicEndpoint config field. SI-2 added a dedicated presignerClient S3Client bound to publicEndpoint in StorageService; getPresignedPartUrl and getPresignedGetUrl now use presignerClient. Server-side send()-based ops (initiate, complete, abort, uploadFile, downloadFile) remain on the internal minio:9000 client. 197 unit+integration tests and 77 E2E tests all green.
implementedFeatures.notes: publicEndpoint fallback chain: S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT || S3_ENDPOINT || 'http://minio:9000' — unset = zero-regression. MinIO validates SigV4 Host header so integration tests cannot rewrite URL hostnames for internal fetches; internalTestClient (S3Client pointing to minio:9000) is created in the integration spec for part uploads. Unit tests use direct config injection (provide: s3Config.KEY, useValue: ...) instead of process.env manipulation. S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000 set in .env for local dev. Manual host-level acceptance test passed 2026-10-26.

implemented: POST /auth/register — register new user (creates user + channel, sends confirmation email)
GET /auth/confirm-email?token= — confirm email with verification token
POST /auth/login — login, returns access_token + refresh_token in the JSON response body (the NestJS API sets no cookies)
POST /auth/refresh — refresh access token using refresh token cookie
POST /auth/logout — invalidate refresh token, clear cookies
GET /auth/me — get current authenticated user info
POST /videos — initiate video creation and multipart upload (SI-03.3)
POST /videos/:publicId/upload/presign-part — presign URL for a multipart upload part; URL now carries public endpoint (SI-03.4 + fix)
POST /videos/:publicId/upload/complete — complete multipart upload & enqueue processing job (SI-03.6)
POST /videos/:publicId/upload/abort — abort multipart upload; clears upload_id without changing status, returns 204 (SI-03.4)
GET /videos/:publicId — public video info; returns id, public_id, title, status, duration, thumbnail_url (presigned, nullable), created_at. Does NOT return channel data (SI-03.9)
GET /videos/:publicId/stream — 302 redirect to presigned GET URL for streaming; URL now carries public endpoint (SI-03.8 + fix)
GET /videos/:publicId/download — 302 redirect to presigned GET URL with attachment header; URL now carries public endpoint (SI-03.8 + fix)

conventionsAndPatterns: Docker Compose service names as hosts for container-to-container traffic — never localhost/127.0.0.1 in config; sole exception is S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT (the signed-URL host for clients OUTSIDE Docker), which server-side S3 calls never use
`docker compose up -d --build` now brings up the full stack from a clean clone (minio-init provisions the bucket, images carry node_modules via baked npm ci, worker resolves the Video relation graph)
NestJS modules: one module per domain; TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Entity]) in each module; forRootAsync only at app/worker root
Config: @nestjs/config with namespaced registerAs(name, () => ({...})) factories — one file per domain in src/config/; injected via ConfigType<typeof xxxConfig> + @Inject(xxxConfig.KEY)
Env validation: Joi schema in src/config/env.validation.ts passed to ConfigModule.forRoot
StorageService S3 client split: internal `client` (endpoint = minio:9000) for all send()-based ops; `presignerClient` (endpoint = config.publicEndpoint) for all getSignedUrl calls
S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT fallback chain: S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT || S3_ENDPOINT || 'http://minio:9000' — unset preserves current behavior
Test file suffixes: .spec.ts (unit), .integration-spec.ts (integration), .e2e-spec.ts (E2E) — Jest filters by regex; integration/e2e run with --runInBand
Unit tests for StorageService use direct config injection (provide: s3Config.KEY, useValue: ...) — not process.env manipulation — for determinism
Integration tests that need a part upload inside Docker use a locally-created internalTestClient (minio:9000) because MinIO validates SigV4 Host and presignedUrls carry localhost:9000
Documentation must describe the real API contract: GET /videos/:publicId returns 7 fields and no channel data — keep prose route tables aligned with openapi.json and the phase-03 plan

Project workflow for any change (incl. doc fixes): research → planning → implement, with artifacts under docs/ before touching targets — skipping it is an automatic-rejection criterion of the MBA challenge
Git Flow: feature/* and bugfix/* branches from dev, merge to dev; dev -> main when stable; never commit directly to main
Definition of Done: relevant + full test suite passes + tsc --noEmit exits 0 + npm run lint passes (for changes that touch code)
